title: Diwali 2026: Five Days From Dhanteras Today to Bhai Dooj on Tuesday
excerpt: The main day, Lakshmi Puja, falls on Sunday, November 8, in the middle of a five-day festival that began Friday with Dhanteras. Here are the dates, what each day marks, and the foods that fill the table.
body:
• Diwali 2026 runs five days, from Dhanteras on Friday, November 6 to Bhai Dooj on Tuesday, November 10.
  • The main day, Lakshmi Puja, falls on Sunday, November 8 — a weekend main day for families in the US and Canada.
  • Each day has its own observance: Dhanteras for prosperity, Kali Chaudas, Lakshmi Puja, Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj for siblings.
  • The table is the centre of the festival: mithai such as coconut ladoos, kaju katli and gulab jamun, plus savoury snacks, are made and shared through the week.

Diwali, the festival of lights, is under way. The five-day festival began on Friday, November 6 with Dhanteras and reaches its main day, Lakshmi Puja, on Sunday, November 8, according to The Old Farmer's Almanac. Because Sunday is the main day this year, families in the United States and Canada get the central evening of the festival on a weekend.

The five days, in order

The festival follows the Hindu lunar calendar, in the month of Kartik, which is why its Gregorian dates shift each year. The main day falls on the new moon, the darkest night of the lunar month. The Almanac lists the 2026 sequence as Dhanteras on Friday, November 6; Kali Chaudas on Saturday, November 7; the main day of Diwali and Lakshmi Puja on Sunday, November 8; Govardhan Puja on Monday, November 9 (Bali Pratipada in the south); and Bhai Dooj on Tuesday, November 10. The Commercial Appeal, setting out the same calendar for Tennessee readers, likewise puts Dhanteras on November 6 and the conclusion on November 10.

Each day carries a distinct observance. Dhanteras is considered an auspicious day for wealth and prosperity, when homes are decorated with diyas, candles and flowers and doorways marked with rangoli. Kali Chaudas is dedicated to purging evil from the home. The third day is devoted to the triumph of light over darkness and is Goddess Lakshmi's birthday, marked by worship, a family feast, exchanges of sweets and fireworks. Govardhan Puja honours Lord Krishna, and Bhai Dooj closes the festival by celebrating the bond between brothers and sisters.

One festival, several traditions

Hindus, Sikhs and Jains all celebrate Diwali, with different stories behind the same theme of good over evil. For Hindus, it marks the return of Prince Rama of Ayodhya after a 14-year exile, with lamps lit to guide his way home. For Sikhs, it represents freedom, marking the release of Guru Hargobind, who refused his own release until the 52 princes imprisoned with him were freed. For Jains, it marks the day Lord Mahavira attained nirvana. On the evening of the main day, celebrants light dozens of candles and clay lamps, called diyas, throughout their homes and in the streets.

What fills the table

Food is prepared in quantity and shared. The Almanac describes the feast as extravagant, with unique dishes and sweets filling the table, and lists Indian-inspired recipes for the festival including an East Indian curry dip, palak panir made with spinach and tofu, a sweet potato lentil coconut curry and coconut ladoos, which it calls a classic Diwali sweet. Homes are decorated with rangoli, intricate designs made with coloured rice, sand or flower petals, to invite Lakshmi to bless the household, and families gather in their best new clothes to eat sweets and special foods, light diyas and pray.

For diaspora families, the practical shape of Diwali 2026 is simple: the cooking and visiting peak on the weekend of November 7-8, with Govardhan Puja on Monday and Bhai Dooj — the day siblings traditionally visit each other — on Tuesday, November 10.
